item.title: DEL-465: OST Platform Enhancements
item.description:
Environmental Protection | Procurement | Intent to Award | Due: 2026-11-06 In plain English (machine-written): The Department of Environmental Protection intends to award a sole-source contract to Hazen and Sawyer for DEL-465, which covers technical support, training and further enhancements to the OST water supply software, with responses due by Nov. 6, 2026.

DEP intends to enter into a Sole Source agreement with Hazen and Sawyer for DEL-465 to provide technical supporting services, training and knowledge transfer and implementation of additional OST platform enhancements. OST is a dynamic water supply system software that is designed to evolve with the addition of new water quality models or expand existing models with new water quality constituents as these became important and/or required to comply with regulations. Ultimately, DEL-465 will improve OST capabilities and flexibility and prepare DEP staff to more effectively, without or with limited external support, maintain and continue improve OST and provide technical/modeling support to NYC Water Supply daily operations, infrastructure repair projects, long-term planning and water supply climate change vulnerability and adaptation assessments, while being better prepared to take on emerging challenges related to NYC water supply. Any firm which believes it can also provide the required service IN THE FUTURE is invited to, so indicated by letter which must be received no later than November 6th , 2026, 5:00 p…

item.title: 82627B0022-BEDC-NR-107: Structural improvements to the North River WRRF
item.description:
Environmental Protection | Procurement | Solicitation | Due: 2026-12-09 In plain English (machine-written): The Department of Environmental Protection is seeking sealed bids from contractors through Dec. 9, 2026, for structural repairs to the aging North River wastewater treatment plant, including steel caisson protection, dock fender replacement, underdeck repairs and ice breaker reconstruction.

The North River WRRF was originally constructed in 1986, was constructed above the Hudson River with a majority of the structure supported by steel caissons driven into the river soil. Numerous structural elements within the North River WRRF have shown signs of aging and significant degradation. The facility requires repair and upgrades to improve its compliance with DEPs standard operating procedures and to continue to provide reliable wastewater treatment operations in accordance with wastewater treatment regulations. Contract NR-107 will implement structural improvements to the North River WRRF. Contract NR-107 comprises four main project elements: steel caisson protection, sludge barge loading dock fender replacement, underdeck repair and improvements, and ice breaker reconstruction. This Competitive Sealed Bid (RFx') is being released through PASSPort, New York Citys online procurement portal. Responses to this RFx should be submitted via PASSPort. item.title: 82627P0002-BEPA: GI-PSE 1-3 Design Services Task Order Contract for Green Infrastructure in NYC Parks & City-owned Street Ends
item.description:
Environmental Protection | Procurement | Solicitation | Due: 2026-11-18 In plain English (machine-written): The Department of Environmental Protection is seeking proposals from design firms for a task order contract to plan green stormwater infrastructure, such as bioretention systems and permeable pavement, in NYC Parks and city-owned street ends, with responses due Nov. 18, 2026.

The City of New York has a combined sewer system serving approximately one third of the city. During rain events, rainfall is transmitted to the water bodies surrounding the City with limited water quality treatment, contributing to water quality impacts in the receiving water bodies. The scope of GI-PSE 1, 2 and 3 contracts are to design an extensive system of GI practices in NYC Parks and Publicly owned street ends to capture and manage stormwater runoff from impervious surfaces top meet Consent Order requirements. These practices include but are not limited to bioretention systems, permeable pavement, synthetic turf, wetlands, green roofs, subsurface detention/retention systems, and/or any combination thereof. This Request for Proposal (RFx) is being released through PASSPort, New York Citys online procurement portal. Responses to this RFx should be submitted via PASSPort. To access the solicitation, vendors should visit the PASSPort Public Portal at https://www.nyc.gov/site/mocs/passport/about-passport.pageand click on the Search Funding Opportunities in PASSPort blue box. item.title: 82626B0054-BEDC-PS-318 Reconstruction of Paerdegat Pumping Station
item.description:
Environmental Protection | Procurement | Solicitation | Due: 2026-12-16 In plain English (machine-written): The Department of Environmental Protection is seeking bids from pre-qualified contractors to reconstruct the Paerdegat Pumping Station in Brooklyn, with responses due Dec. 16, 2026.

PS-318: Reconstruction of Paerdegat Pumping Station Paerdegat pumping station is located in Brooklyn, New York at 6002 Flatlands Ave, Brooklyn, New York that flows to the Coney Island Wastewater Resource Recovery Facility. The Pumping Station was constructed in 1932 with an upgrade completed in 1995. The station currently has a designed flow capacity of 57 million gallons per day (MGD) wet weather flow and 22.8 MGD dry weather flow. The existing station is in need of State of Good Repair (SOGR) upgrades in order to improve compliance with DEPs SOPs and design guidelines. Specifically, areas needing SOGR improvements include replacing existing pumps, placing wet well elevation monitoring system, new mechanical, HVAC, electrical, I&C systems, resiliency upgrades, provide permanent emergency fuel generator and fuel storage, replace crane electrification system, rehab wet well structure, reconstruction of floors, walls, and ceilings, replace clay tile and membrane roofing, replace building façade walls, windows, floors, and brick fence, replace plumbing and fixtures in bathroom, replace existing force main, install new parallel force main, extend spillway, replace the gate wall thim…

item.title: New York City Indirect Source Rule 'WISER' Program
item.description:
Environmental Protection | Public Hearings and Meetings | Meeting | Hearing: 2026-11-17 In plain English (machine-written): The Department of Environmental Protection will hold a virtual public scoping meeting on Nov. 17, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. to take comments on a draft scope for its proposed Warehouse Indirect Source Emissions Reduction program, which would require large warehouse operators to reduce pollution from mobile sources or offset air pollution from their operations.

New York City Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) proposes to implement a Warehouse Indirect Source Emissions Reduction (WISER) local law that would require large warehouse operators to reduce mobile sources of pollution and/or mitigate the impact of the air pollution associated with their operations in New York City. In accordance with the State Environmental Quality Review Act (SEQRA) (Section 8-0113, Article 8 of the Environmental Conservation Law) as set forth in 6 NYCRR Part 617, and the City Environmental Quality Review (CEQR) process, as set forth in Executive Order 91 of 1977 and its amendments, DEP is hereby issuing Notice of Positive Declaration, Intent to Prepare a Draft Environmental Impact Statement, Lead Agency Declaration and Draft Scope of Work.

DEP will hold a virtual public scoping meeting to receive public comments on the Draft Scope of Work on November 17, 2026, at 4:00 PM. The Draft Scope of Work, which provides a summary description of the Program and the methodologies to be used in prep…
